lines.en: label futabaspring2:
scene sky
A long time ago, I used to visit the library pretty frequently. And one of the key reasons for that was how Futaba was among the most...accepting of my advances early on.
Of course, I would subsequently learn that a great deal of that was the result of her nearly-absent self-esteem. But it’s not like I knew that immediately.
It took a few visits first. And in those first few visits, I learned that there is and was far more to her than just the flaws she gets hung up on.
There’s a girl in there who wants to succeed and wants to be recognized. But the one she wants to be recognized by is herself rather than me.
Well, she definitely wants to be recognized by me too. But I have “recognized” her many times by now and she is still unhappy, so I imagine I’m in second place at best.
Regardless, I think back on these days as I swallow my pride and return to the halls I used to wander on a daily basis.
scene futabatree1
And what I find is that same girl, enduring that same struggle she suffered so long ago in trying to put her feelings onto paper.
And I can’t help but wonder if she’s gotten better now that I have forced her into feeling everything one possibly can before even finishing her first year of high school.
Writing is hard, though. Describing how you feel is hard. And there are only so many words you can do it with, which makes it even harder.
: Mnh...
I guess there’s a good chance she’s just writing smut instead, though. Since that seems to be what she’s most interested in now that she has discovered the joys of elf sex.
: This is...much harder than I thought it would be. Maybe I should try a different story instead?
: Talent in the world of writing doesn’t come immediately, Futaba. It’s a skill that’s acquired as time goes on.

: For example — Mark Twain didn’t write the Adventures of Huckleberry Finn until he was almost 50 years old. Which means he must have gotten good at writing sometime after that since that book sucked.
: That doesn’t help me at all, Sensei. Not when the deadline for submissions is-
scene futabatree2
: Wait, Sensei? When did you get here? I didn’t even hear you walk in.
: Probably because you’re so absorbed in whatever you’re working on. Which may or may not be smut.
scene futabatree3
: It’s not smut. I know better than to write things like that in school.
: Didn’t you give me a boob job in the nurse’s office once?
scene futabatree4
: She was off that day. Which means I did nothing wrong.
: Is she off today too? Want to drop what you’re doing and go relive some happy memories?
scene futabatree5
: As nostalgic as it sounds to help get you off after you went through the trouble of coming all the way over here, I can’t right now. I have to finish this story by tonight or I miss my chance.
: Your chance to what? Is Wakana holding another writing contest or something?
: Miss Watabe isn’t, but there’s a contest I found online to put a creative spin on a children’s book. So I’ve been working on that all week.
: Oh yeah? Can I see what you have done?
scene futabatree6
: It might not be as pleasurable as my first suggestion, but grading your unfinished writing is still nostalgic in its own way, is it not?
: It is...It’s just my first time trying to...parody something, so to speak. And I’m worried that what I do have will look pretty terrible compared to the original story.
: What’s the original story? Which children’s book are you trying to put a spin on?
: The Giving Tree by Shel Silverstein.
scene futabatree7
: Well, on the bright side, it’ll be hard for you to write anything even remotely as depressing as that.
: You think The Giving Tree is depressing, Sensei?
: A tree spends its entire existence catering to an ungrateful boy who ultimately chops it down and turns it into a boat? It’d take a fool to think something like that is happy.
scene futabatree8
: Well, I guess you can call me a fool then. Because I don’t think it’s as sad as you’re making it sound.
: Of course you don’t. Because you’re in that bracket of people who don’t mind sacrificing themselves for others even when it means you’re going to wind up hurting.
: And you’re in that bracket of people who don’t mind chopping down a tree you’ve grown up with so long as it benefits you in some way.
: You’re right. You don’t need to worry about me turning you into a boat, though. We’d probably just both drown if I tried to do that.
scene futabatree9
: Well, what would you try to do, Sensei? Because I think your outlook might be really helpful here since I’m trying to approach this story from the opposite angle.
: You mean, like...a “Taking Tree” instead of a “Giving Tree?”
: Exactly. And it’s from the perspective of the boy instead this time, who sees the tree more like a curse than something beneficial to him.
: I’ve obviously had to change a few things in order for it to make sense, but the format is the same. And I got Maya to help me draw some of the pictures to keep the kids entertained.
: Maya can draw? Since when?
scene futabatree10
: Since always, I think. I’m surprised you didn’t know.
: She actually used to draw quite a bit for the manga club until Molly started making too many demands and Maya stopped just to spite her.
: Yeah, that tracks. Aren’t you worried a story like this might be too dark for kids, though? Like, what’s the takeaway supposed to be in a book about a cursed tree?
scene futabatree11
: The takeaway is supposed to be that there are always going to be things out there that want to hurt you.
: And yeah, I guess that might be a little dark for a children’s book. But it’s an important theme to explore, I think.
: And it might help some kids understand bullying a little better if they ever have to experience that. Which...they probably will. Most people do.
: Were you ever bullied, Sensei?
scene futabatree12
: Not really. But anyway, if that’s the angle you want to go with, I’m sure it’s doable. Especially with your outlook and...experience in the subject matter.
: Yes, I’m a bit of an expert in the field of being bullied, aren’t I?
: Just means you’re stronger now.
: It doesn’t really. That is the approach I’m taking from a writer’s perspective, though — showing how years of the tree’s curse sort of help the boy build up an immunity to it.
: How exactly does a tree take something, though?
: I mean, it’s not like it’s physically taking anything. But it looms over his house, and every time  he sees its shadow cross into his yard, something bad happens.
: That’s not the tree’s fault though, is it? It can’t control its own shadow.
: No, but the boy is just a boy. So he doesn’t know that. Which is why he gives the tree an evil voice whenever he visits it to ask it to leave him alone.
: Then, by the time he’s old enough to understand how shadows work, he’s already associated the tree with horrible things happening. Hence the “curse.”
: I see...
scene futabatree13
: You hate it, don’t you?
: No, I don’t hate it. I haven’t even read it yet. It’s just...do you think something like this would have helped you when you were little?
: Because if it’s from the boy’s perspective and it’s all just cursing this tree that isn’t really doing anything, it’s sort of just...the Giving Tree again but with different, sadder narration.
scene futabatree14
: Yeah...that’s exactly my problem. No matter what I do, I can’t figure out how to actually make the tree evil. And the boy keeps forgiving it in the end.
: But that’s not what I want. I want him to hate it. And I want him to chop it down and...get revenge for all of the terrible things it did but...didn’t really do...
: But you know that wouldn’t send the message you want to send...
scene futabatree15
: Right...Which is why I keep thinking it might be better to just try and use a different story instead. But I really like this one and...I don’t know.
: Maybe it’s just me not being as good of a writer as I want to be yet? Like, if I can’t get the simplest idea across in the simplest format, what does that say about my skill?
: Have I learned nothing at all this whole time? How come I still suck while people like Nodoka can just write whatever they want and make it sound good?
scene futabatree16
: Comparing yourself to gifted people like that will always be a recipe for disaster, Futaba...
: Nodoka’s a very special and very rare type of person. But it’s important to remember that people like that struggle even harder sometimes because they don’t have anyone to relate to.
scene futabatree17
: You and I are lucky we understand one another. We’re lucky we can sit here and identify the cracks in your story when Nodoka likely wouldn’t even recognize them as cracks at all.
scene futabatree18
: That’s...fair.
: Do you and I really understand one another, though?
: As much as we can, I think. With plenty of room for error, of course. I don’t know if it’s possible to ever really fully understand someone.
: I just know that if you’re trying to force an idea across, it’s not going to work. It’ll come off as preachy...or inauthentic...or even worse — it could come off as Huckleberry Finn.
scene futabatree19
: Why am I just learning today that you have such great disdain for Huckleberry Finn?
: Why am I just learning today that you are trying to write behind my back when I am supposed to be your writing coach? We had an agreement.
: Did we? Why am I learning right now that you actually care about my writing? I figured you gave up on that once we started having sex.
: That came out meaner than I wanted it to. I’m sorry.
scene futabatree20
: Don’t be. You’re clearly not the only one here struggling to get their feelings across. And I’m sure it hasn’t helped at all that I just walked away from school entirely.
: I don’t actually blame you for writing “behind my back.” I was just being a facetious douche again.
scene futabatree21
: Wait, are you okay? Because I suddenly feel really bad about saying what I said if that’s your response to it.
: Are you okay? Because if you’ve spent the last week wanting to murder a fictional tree for revenge, I can’t imagine you’re the same Futaba I’ve been jerking off to this whole time.
scene futabatree22
: That came out lewder than I wanted it to. I’m sorry.
: Don’t be. I was masturbating to you before we ever even talked.
: That makes me feel a lot better. Thank you, Futaba.
scene futabatree23
: What are we going to do about your story, though? It needs to be done by tonight, doesn’t it?
: You don’t need to do anything, Sensei. I’ll probably just go with my gut and finish “The Giving Tree Pt. II” and hope no one else submitted anything for the contest.
: But maybe soon, I can try writing something...original again. And you can read that and tell me more about how inadequate it is or...what I need to change.
scene futabatree24
: Futaba, you’re a teenager. You don’t need to be perfect. It would be weird if everything you wrote was adequate. Having to change things is completely normal. For professionals too.
: I know...I know. I just...kind of need to win this. And that pressure isn’t...meshing well with everything else that’s been going on in my head lately.
: Why do you...need to win a children’s book writing contest exactly?
: Futaba-
: I need the money.
scene black
: I’m trying to go to America.
scene futabatree25
: You really still haven’t heard anything from your parents? It’s been, like...over a year, hasn’t it?
: That’s why I want to go find them. It’s, like...super weird. And unnerving. They’ve always trusted me to be independent, but they’ve never just...left me alone for this long before.
: But...money won’t be enough to get you to there. You know that, right? There’s still the matter of the barrier and-
: I just have to figure out how to get through it. You did once, didn’t you?
: I don’t...really know. I just remember following Nodoka and...that’s pretty much it.
: Still, there has to be a way...there has to.
: Don’t you think people are too...accepting of this? Being stuck here? Just...living our lives, completely unsure of when and if we’ll ever be allowed to leave again?
scene futabatree26
: Don’t you want to know what’s out there, Sensei?...
: What we’re missing?...
: I...do. But there are things about this world that don’t exactly make sense. So I’m hesitant to-
: Don’t you want to know what’s out there, Sensei?...
: What we’re missing?...
scene futabatree27
: Sensei?
: How am I supposed to respond to that when you’ll just ignore anything I have to say?...
: What? Why would I-
: I don’t think it’s safe out there, Futaba. I think you should stay here. With me.
: Sensei...But my parents-
: What if you can’t find them?
: What if something happened?
: Then what, Futaba?...
: Then I find out what it was...
: I can’t just keep waiting around, though...
: I’ve already tried that...and it’s driving me insane.
: I can’t take it anymore, Sensei...
: I need something...
: Anything...
: And I’m not going to find any of that in this town.
scene colorbars
scene black
